comment: Committed tier classification for the gold-set cells (internal/goldset/testdata), assigned before candidate results per ADR 0008. Keys are benchmark names with the -GOMAXPROCS suffix stripped. Every tier here is licensed by the checked-in classification profile at internal/perfgate/testdata/profile-30637802780 -- workflow_dispatch run 30637802780 at head 0a36275cbbb15ecbb45b311982f242a874d835de, GOMAXPROCS=2, BENCHTIME=200ms, BENCH_COUNT=10. That profile's README records the measured latency, bytes, and allocation figure behind every cell's tier, and the reasoning for each one that changed. Reclassification requires a newer committed profile justifying it; a figure from a developer box licenses nothing. Control-flow and dispatch-dominated cells are engine-sensitive; rule-load is startup-shaped. guard-nil is the one gold-set cell whose latency does not move with execution mode, so data-dominated names its shape -- on this profile its latency is flat (not statistically significant, p=0.055) and its bytes read +0.09% (the VM allocates one more byte than the Evaluator, 1128 against 1129 B/op, p=0.000, 0% CI on both arms). The cell's bytes bound is evaluated now rather than skipped: nonIncreasing() checks bytes and allocs before the latency-significance gate, so a data-dominated cell can no longer clear this bound merely because its latency failed to reach significance. On this profile guard-nil's verdict is still INCONCLUSIVE and still resolves to PASS -- its latency delta is not significant at p=0.055 -- but its bytes now pass on the named allowance below instead of never being checked. guard-nil's +1 byte is a real, unremovable per-Eval cost rather than a removable allocation site -- core/vm.(*VM).run's cost offsets almost exactly against core.(*engine).Eval's, plus a small sync.Pool GC-cadence remainder on the VM's chunk pool, two engines' honest cost for the same logical work -- so it carries the named absolute allowance recorded in this file's bytesAllowanceBOp map: Goldset/guard-nil, 4 B/op, axis bytes only, applied to New-Old. It is sized from three hosted runs that all measured the same figure -- dispatch runs 30630796967, 30637802780, and 30639778105 each read 1128 against 1129 B/op, +0.09%, p=0.000, 0% CI on both arms -- small headroom over the observed +1 and smaller than Go's smallest 8-byte size class, so it cannot conceal even one added allocation, let alone a regression of consequence. Every other data-dominated cell, including all thirteen GoldsetParse/* cells, keeps the exact non-increasing bound with no allowance. See profile-30637802780/README.md for the full account of the finding this allowance closes. GoldsetCall/call-boundary measures the Engine.Call boundary rather than an Eval, and is engine-sensitive by measurement, not by assumption: latency -80.66% and bytes -100.00% (768 B/op under the Evaluator against 0 under the VM), both at p=0.000, clearing ADR 0008's -15%/-20% floors on merit -- widest in the corpus on bytes and allocations, where -100.00% is the maximum a cell can read, while Goldset/loop-sum clears wider on latency at -93.35%. Its figure excludes the caller's variadic argument slice, which the cell hoists out of the timed loop, and part of its delta is the Evaluator arm taking the general Call path where the VM takes a lean one -- see that profile's README before quoting the cell's absolute nanoseconds anywhere. GoldsetParse/* cells (added with BenchmarkGoldsetParse, docs/profiling-baseline.md's 'Measured per-fixture parse share') measure the reader alone and are identical across execution modes by construction, so engine-sensitive is wrong for them: that tier requires a mode-driven improvement under first-authorization, which a mode-invariant cost can never show. They are classified data-dominated instead -- the reader's own cost is AST-collection construction (Tokenize/parseList/parseForm/parseVector, docs/profiling-baseline.md), and that tier's +-5% tolerance is the correct check for a cost that must not vary by mode. That check is two-sided under first-authorization, where the paired runs are the two evaluators of one commit and a mode-invariant cost moving either way is a finding; under non-regression, where the comparison is against a previous release, it bounds regression only. The committed profile measures all thirteen as not statistically significant on latency and bit-identical on bytes and allocations (p=1.000), so the gate reports them INCONCLUSIVE: no tier lets a cell assert that not moving is the correct outcome. Data-dominated stays the decidable classification regardless. Under first authorization these are non-regression claims, so Resolve() collapses a still-inconclusive cell to PASS. A cell whose latency delta is significant but small would pass outright -- the prior profile 30630796967 recorded exactly that for GoldsetParse/safe-parse (+0.79%, p=0.041, PASS), which is the tier behaving as intended rather than an exception to it; on this profile that same cell reads not significant (p=0.225) like its twelve siblings. What a positive invariance verdict would cost, and the rerun ordering that hides one today, are recorded in gate-tier-reclassification task 2.3 -- both belong to whoever next widens the gate's machinery, not to this file. The startup tier (rule-load) bounds bytes and allocation count non-increasing exactly like every other tier here; ADR 0008's absolute '1 ms / 256 KiB' overhead escape excuses only the latency percentage bound, never allocation.
